name: Md. Code, Environment § 9-331.1 (sewer overflow and treatment plant bypass reporting and public notification)
waters_covered: all surface and ground waters of the State
access_detail: Statute text page fetched (raw/statute-env-9-331.1.html). Amended by 2019 HB 417, Chapter 310, effective October 1, 2019 (bill page raw/hb0417-2019.html).
status_reason: Primary legal basis: 24-hour report to MDE, 5-day written report, and the 2019 posting duties (site sign in Spanish and English; MDE, MDH and local health department websites; health department social media).
notes: Quote (a)(2): "The report shall be made as soon as practicable but no later than 24 hours after the time that the operator or owner became aware of the event." (b)(2)(i) requires the procedures to require that the notification be posted "1. In Spanish and English at the location of the sewer overflow or treatment plant bypass; 2. On the website of the Department, the Maryland Department of Health, and the appropriate local health department; and 3. On any social media website on which the appropriate local health department regularly posts information". (b)(2)(ii) adds notice "within a reasonable time" to downstream jurisdictions, county governments, impacted State parks, DNR and other land managers. (c)(1) health departments make all public-health determinations. COMAR 26.08.10 (2005) has not been amended to carry the 2019 website duties (its administrative history lists only the 2005 adoption).

name: COMAR 26.08.10 Overflows or Bypasses (reports to MDE and local health department; public notification)
operator: Maryland Department of the Environment (regulation); Division of State Documents (publisher)
access_detail: Full chapter fetched (raw/comar-26.08.10-full.html, text raw/comar-26.08.10.txt). The dsd.maryland.gov/regulations/Pages/26.08.10.xx.aspx URLs now redirect to regs.maryland.gov.
license: Site footer: "This version of the laws and codes on this website is licensed under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license with copyright held by the State of Maryland. This version of the laws and codes on this website will be dedicated to the public domain under the CC0 1.0 license 180 days after publication." and "Please do not scrape. Instead, bulk download".
legal_basis: COMAR 26.08.10.01-.11; effective March 28, 2005 (32:6 Md. R. 636); authority Environment Article §9-331.1
status_reason: Defines overflow, the 24-hour telephone report to MDE and the local health department (.03C), 5-day written report (.05A), the 24-hour public notice for overflows entering shellfish, drinking-water, bathing-beach or public-recreation waters (.08A), the 10,000-gallon notice and posting rule (.08C), the advisory duration (.08D) and the notice content (.08F).
notes: .03C: "Reports required by this chapter shall be made by telephone as soon as practicable to the telephone number or numbers designated by the Department, but not later than 24 hours after the time that the owner or operator becomes aware of the event." .08A: "... the owner or operator shall notify the public as soon as practicable, but not later than 24 hours after the time that the owner or operator becomes aware of the event, about: (1) Any overflow that enters: (a) Shellfish harvesting waters; (b) Waters protected as drinking water sources; (c) Waters used as public bathing beaches where people may swim; or (d) Waters used for public recreation where people may boat, fish, or swim". .08C: "if the overflow's total volume at the time of completed repair as measured or estimated using best professional judgment is 10,000 gallons or more, the owner or operator shall notify the public by: (1) A public service announcement or paid advertising in a daily newspaper, radio station, or television station ... and (2) Posting affected areas" (no separate deadline stated in .08C). .08D: advisory stays "until ... sampling data for the receiving water shows return to normal or prior background levels." .08E: under 10,000 gallons with no .08B factors, notice may be via quarterly/annual reports, water bills or a web site. Exclusion .01B(3)(a): 50 gallons or less to the ground cleaned up within 1 hour. The .03C 'by telephone' wording predates 2019 Ch. 310, which repealed the telephone requirement in statute.

estimate_flag (not a field; the description says volumes may be estimates)
cadence: Metadata 'Update Frequency: Daily'; the MDE web page says 'currently updated monthly'. Observed: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-11-02 15:55:53 UTC and every row's :created_at = 2026-11-02T15:55:47Z (full table replaced), newest row an SSO starting 2026-11-01 07:00, so latency about one day after the event. Legal: 24-hour report to MDE, 5-day written report.
history: This table: overflows from February 2023 onward (description says 'February 10th, 2023, onward'; min start_date 2023-01-04). Earlier records 2005-01 to 2023-01 in the frozen dataset md-mde-sewer-overflows-2005-2023.
license: Socrata metadata: license 'Public Domain' (licenseId PUBLIC_DOMAIN); attribution 'Maryland Department of the Environment'.
status_reason: The only statewide, daily, machine-readable event table; covers CSO, SSO, plant bypass and unauthorized discharges with NPDES number and volume. Build against it first.
notes: Quality notes from 2025-2026 rows: (1) `id` is a sort-order number (id 1 = newest) re-issued each reload, and the Socrata system :id is regenerated too (all rows share one :created_at). Dedupe on npdes_no+start_date+start_time+overflow_address. (2) Duplicate rows for one event exist (e.g. 2025-01-24 Jones Falls 4,191,760 gal twice; 2025-07-10 Gwynns Falls 400,225/400,125). (3) lat/long sometimes swapped (2025-02-13 Deepdene Rd lat -76.6342) and overflow_longitude is typed text. (4) receiving_water is free text: 'none', 'storm drain', 'Gwynns Falls is about 500 feet away'; 923 rows null/none/N/A/unknown. (5) discharge_volume can be an early figure that the operator later revises (Baltimore DPW layer shows 17,520 gal where MDE shows 11,000 for 500 W University Pkwy 2026-10-27). (6) False alarms stay in: WSSC's 2026-10-26 Westbard Ave report is stamped NON-REPORTABLE (0 gal) but the MDE row remains. (7) A 2026-10-11 Perryville row repeats cause text naming 'Tropical Storm Isaias' (a 2020 storm), i.e. copied text. (8) 455 rows since 2025-01-01 are 10,000 gal or more. penalty_id present on 558 rows.
